column1: # Game profile of Subnautica: Below Zero (Switch, update 1.23.55063 = v655360). Plays on the Mac
# Unity 2019.4.36f1 (IL2CPP) with FMOD, SDK 13.3.5 (its sdk and movie module are AI: THE SOMNIUM FILES - nirvanA Initiative's builds, which already carry the node-area cut).
# The shaders are Unity's Shader and ComputeShader objects in the player's serialized files and the 14,633 bundles in StreamingAssets/aa/Switch, read by unityfs.py with
# Unity 2019.4's layouts (10,840 shaders, 11 of them the player's GLSLC outputs in main)
# The game sets present interval 2 in play and runs at 30 fps as on the Switch

# Game name: only a label for profile listings and the Mac window title; the iOS app name is the game name in the base NSP, and the bundle ID comes from the base game title ID (build_ipa.sh / NSP script)
# first-person 3D: the right stick looks around
# load order as on Horizon: main, subsdk*, sdk (subsdk0 = NintendoSDK_movie)
# The NPDM declares 8 MB of system resource, so IsVirtualAddressMemoryEnabled is true: nninitStartup hands application pool − used memory to StandardAllocator as
# virtual address memory and never sets a heap. With the hardware pool the alias region was used up to +4.28 GB of 4.38 GB within a second of nnMain (the NSP script's
# heap check), so a 1 GB pool and the 5 GB block (256 MB in front + 4.375 GB alias region + 256 MB stack region + 128 MB heap region), as for nirvanA Initiative
